reasons: The open question is the secondary eclipse. secondary_depth_ppm 91 +/- 16 is a 5.7 sigma detection, 2.2 sigma above secondary_maximum_planet_depth_ppm 56, and is 49% of fit_depth_ppm 185 — the ratio a diluted eclipsing binary gives. It cannot be an undiluted EB on the target because fit_radius_ratio 0.0120 +/- 0.00102 is far too small for a star, transit_grazing is False, and gaia_rv_companion_mass_upper_limit_solar_masses 0.15 excludes a stellar companion; so if the secondary is real the signal is a blend, and if it is systematics the candidate is a planet. The data cannot tell: the phase-curve errors are demonstrably underestimated (ellipsoidal_amplitude_ppm_by_sector S6 +68 +/- 29 versus S32 -166 +/- 25 disagree by ~6 sigma; net ellipsoidal_amplitude_ppm -69 +/- 18 has the unphysical sign and ellipsoidal_companion_mass_solar_masses is empty), and the phase-0.5 panel of the all-sector figure shows only unbinned scatter.

The blend scenario is not excluded by the pixel or TRICERATOPS checks. gaia_neighbours_able_to_cause_dip lists Gaia DR3 3222832580043050240 at 15" (G 17.8, needs 30%) and Gaia DR3 3222831828423617536 / 3222831828424528512 at 21" (G 17.2 needs 16%, G 17.7 needs 27%) — ordinary EB eclipse depths, and all within one 21" pixel of the target. pixel_verdicts_by_sector gives on-target only in S98 at SNR 6.1; S6 (SNR 2.7) and S32 (SNR 1.5) are too faint, and their difference images are jitter dipoles with the best star on other Gaia sources. A single SNR-6 centroid cannot separate a 15" neighbour. nearby_scenarios_excluded True with nfpp_mean 0 and nfpp_standard_deviation 0 means the nearby-star scenarios were removed on the strength of that pixel verdict, so fpp_mean 0.08973 does not test them; joint_difference_image_snr and joint_pixel_verdict are empty.

Two weaker indicators lean the same way but are not decisive. The transit is shorter than the target star predicts: fitted_to_expected_scaled_semi_major_axis 1.55 and stellar_density_fit_to_tic_ratio 1.69, with fit_scaled_semi_major_axis 2.40 +/- 0.353 about 2 sigma above the expected value — mildly favouring a smaller, denser host, as a blend on a faint neighbour would give. And depth_ppm_by_sector S6 101 +/- 38 is 2.2 sigma shallower than S98 202 +/- 24 and S32 190 +/- 29 (sector_depth_consistency_p_value 0.0723), matching the lower-than-expected S6 SNR in other_sector_results (SNR 6.3 versus expected 8.6). The cutout apertures (cutout_depth_ppm_by_sector_and_aperture S98 r1.5 204 to r3.0 227; S32 225 to 229) do not show aperture-dependent depth, which argues against a blend, so this is balanced.

The candidate is not a drop. It is independently detected: other_sector_results S32 SPOC SNR 8.8 (expected 10.0), joint_search_snr 11.7 against joint_search_highest_null_snr 7.6, joint_search_detected True, joint_search_period_days 0.634005 matching fit_period_days 0.6340068 +/- 0.00000132. odd_even_difference_sigma 0.48 (odd_depth_ppm 171, even_depth_ppm 187) rules out an EB at twice the period. planet_radius_earth_radii 2.64 +/- 0.24 is far below the 22.4 Earth-radius stellar limit and the radius is constrained (transit_grazing False, fit_impact_parameter 0.403 +/- 0.2668). gaia_ruwe 0.89, gaia_non_single_star 0, gaia_eclipsing_binary False, vsx_binaries empty. exofop_tois, exofop_ctois and published_signal are empty and the record states no TOI, CTOI, TCE or TESS EB match in the catalogues of 2026-10-15. triceratops_verdict is 'likely planet' with most_likely_scenario 'TP on TIC 220073982'.

Host-star caution to carry forward: gaia_vbroad_km_s 340.76 on stellar_radius_solar_radii 2.01042 implies a rotation period no longer than ~0.30 d (2*pi*R/v), about half the candidate period, and near break-up for a star of this size; gaia_rv_amplitude_robust_km_s 46.24, gaia_rv_epoch_scatter_km_s 14.7 and gaia_rv_chisq_pvalue 0.011 (gaia_rv_variable False) show the RVs are poor. Either vbroad is spurious or the TIC parameters are off, and in either case RV confirmation will be impractical. This does not decide the case but should be noted in any eventual submission.

What decides it: unreleased_tess_sectors_observing_the_star is 110. When Sector 110 is released, re-run the all-sector verification with S110 included and (a) check whether secondary_depth_ppm stays above secondary_maximum_planet_depth_ppm at more than ~3 sigma with per-sector phase-curve values that agree — then propose for drop as a blended eclipsing binary — or falls within the planetary maximum — then propose for submission; and (b) run the joint S98+S110 difference image (joint_difference_image_snr, joint_best_source) to test the 15" and 21" neighbours against TIC 220073982. released_tess_sectors_not_in_all_sector_verification and other_sectors_absent are empty, so nothing already released is waiting.

Disagreement with the mechanical decision ('proposed for submission: no rule holds or drops it') and with the earlier agent entry in the verification record, which stated that 'held' does not apply because all released sectors are used. The instructions name a sector that TESS observes and has not released as a hold trigger, and Sector 110 bears directly on the only open question (secondary eclipse / blend). Submitting now would put a CTOI on ExoFOP with a 5.7 sigma secondary exceeding the planetary limit and with the nearest neighbours untested; waiting for one sector costs little. If Sector 110 is not released within a reasonable time or does not resolve it, submit with the secondary eclipse and the rapid-rotator host flagged for ground-based photometric follow-up of the 15" and 21" neighbours.
